title: fix(doctor): avoid stack overflows during retained history recovery
body:
Refs #179481

## What Problem This Solves

Large retained-history inventories can still exceed Node's function-argument limit during Doctor session repair. The alias resolver was already fixed by #162321; the remaining failures come from spreading entire registries, recovery findings, restore results, and warnings into `push`.

## User Impact

Doctor preserves complete archived ownership and recovery diagnostics without a stack overflow. Import, recovery, and restore keep the same ordering, warning content, backup protection, and current-session ownership rules. There are no schema, dependency, or CLI changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Append unbounded collections one item at a time, and reuse freshly created result arrays where no append is needed. The neighborhood audit also covers legacy-main comparison claims and warning presentation. Remaining argument spreads on this path are bounded by the 256-entry import batch or a one-item producer.

The registry overflow was previously caught and turned into a deferred-history warning, losing the recovered ownership inventory. The settlement-issue overflow escapes `runDoctorSessionSqlite`, matching the failure class caught as `blocked-by-session-repair-failure`. The reporter did not provide an inner stack, and the large settlement-failure population in the regression is synthetic; this PR therefore references the issue rather than claiming its exact production cause is proven.

## Evidence

- Added two 500,000-entry regressions at production boundaries: archived ownership discovery resolves the final registry owner, and the Doctor import entry point retains all settlement findings.
- Unmodified Node 26.12.0: both regressions fail; the second throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` at the issue append in `runDoctorSessionSqlite`. Fixed Node 26.12.1: 2/2 pass (1.8 seconds test time). Repository-pinned Bun 1.4.4: 2/2 pass (0.8 seconds test time); Bun also accepted the original large argument lists.
- Real filesystem/source-command proof: a 56,777,781-byte archived registry with 500,000 entries and one retained transcript completed Doctor dry-run and import. Import reported one entry, two transcript events, and zero issues. SQLite retained `agent:main:dashboard:499999`; original archive hashes still match their receipts. The source harness invoked `doctorCommand` through `runCliWithExitFinalization` with isolated HOME, state, and config. The normal development launcher refused runtime-artifact publication while it could not establish that the managed Gateway was offline; no operator Gateway was stopped or modified.
- Targeted Doctor typecheck, touched-file oxlint/oxfmt, and Madge (zero cycles) pass. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Integrated current main's structured Doctor findings change after resolving its overlapping warning renderer. The affected four-file regression run passes (23 tests, 31.71 seconds including preparation); targeted Doctor typecheck, touched-file lint, and a fresh independent review also pass on the merged candidate.
- Executed all 89 importing-consumer files. The final 59-file group passed on Node 26.12.1 (610 tests passed, two skipped). Earlier groups exposed a daemon-runtime mismatch under host Node 26.12.0, which passes on 26.12.1, and one existing Darwin fixture failure: `agent-create.integration.test.ts` / `stops delegated creation after authority closes during workspace-write preparation` reports `no such table: migration_sources` after disabling the native filesystem helper. The same failure reproduces on untouched base production sources under Node 26.12.1. No test was skipped or weakened to hide it. The Windows-only suite remains platform-skipped on macOS.

<details>
<summary>Focused commands</summary>

All state-capable commands ran with isolated `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` under the task worktree.

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.scale.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.scale.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.commands-doctor.json --incremental
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-madge-import-cycles.ts
```

The filesystem proof used a task-local fixture builder, then `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/run-live.ts import`. The harness called the public `doctorCommand(undefined, { sessionSqlite: "import", sessionSqliteAllAgents: true, json: true })` through the normal `runCliWithExitFinalization` owner. It used only the synthetic state directory and config, with no mocked readers.

</details>
- Full `check:changed`, including its slow SQLite inventory, was not run under the campaign's local gate budget; PR CI supplies broad proof.
- Production: +63/-49 lines; tests: +119/-0; documentation: +6/-1.

### Reporter Q2: abandoning retained inputs

`openclaw update cleanup --dry-run` previews eligible rollback originals. After stopping the Gateway and database readers, `openclaw update cleanup` (or `openclaw update cleanup --yes --json`) permanently retires eligible, verified originals. It is not a force-abandon command: incomplete, unverified, or protected recovery inputs remain protected. Database-bound receipts also remain protected until a later completed update. There is no supported command to forget arbitrary unresolved/foreign-receipt inputs. Whether to provide that explicit data-loss escape hatch remains a design question for Peter; none is added here.

Sources: [cleanup command](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0f5ec1bd02ae3d859148da561d10d4e5b3a72785/src/cli/update-cli/cleanup.ts#L57-L67), [maintenance ownership](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0f5ec1bd02ae3d859148da561d10d4e5b3a72785/src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-retirement.ts#L198), and [eligibility protections](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0f5ec1bd02ae3d859148da561d10d4e5b3a72785/src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-recovery-inventory.ts#L198-L223).

### Reporter Q3: online inspect/validate

Yes: `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite inspect` and `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite validate` are logical read-only operations and do not take the exclusive maintenance lease. [Doctor dispatch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0f5ec1bd02ae3d859148da561d10d4e5b3a72785/src/commands/doctor.ts#L93-L104) applies the lock only to [import, compact, restore, and recover](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0f5ec1bd02ae3d859148da561d10d4e5b3a72785/src/commands/doctor-sqlite-maintenance-lock.ts#L141-L143). [Session database readers](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0f5ec1bd02ae3d859148da561d10d4e5b3a72785/src/infra/session-sqlite-migration-readers.ts#L461-L477) open with `readOnly: true` and close afterward. Validation can add load; separate reads can observe different commits while the Gateway runs. SQLite readers may touch WAL/SHM sidecars. Avoid running cleanup concurrently.
